newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES WIN SUBWAY SERIES IN 10TH ON MARTINEZ HIT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES WIN SUBWAY SERIES IN 10TH ON MARTINEZ HIT.

text.p: Tino Martinez's one-out single in the bottom of the 10th inning brought Paul O'Neill home for a 3-2 Yankee victory over the Mets and New York City bragging rights Wednesday.

O'Neill had drawn a walk from Greg McMichael (3-6) and took third on a single by Cecil Fielder before Mets closer John Franco faced Martinez. Hitless in his last 21 at-bats, Martinez slapped a 1-2 pitch to left, easily scoring O'Neill.
"It was a fastball over the outer half of the plate, and I just went with it," said Martinez.
"This is the first time I've ever seen John Franco."

The Yankees took the final two games of the "Subway Series" after the Mets posted a 6-0 shutout in the opener. The three-game set drew 168,719 fans, the most at Yankee Stadium since it was reopened in 1976. The series finale drew 56,278.

Mike Stanton (3-0) picked up the win with two scoreless innings of relief of ex-Met David Cone, who had a no-hitter into the seventh until John Olerud doubled. One out later, Olerud took third on a wild pitch and scored on a groundout.
"It's the second time Olerud broke up a no-hitter of mine," said Cone, "leading off with the same type of hit. If we lost this game, I would've taken a cyanide tablet."
The Mets scored their second run on a Cone balk with pinch-runner Steve Bieser on third.
The Yankees had a Joe Girardi home run taken away in the fifth after it was first called fair, then foul.
Chad Curtis homered for the Yankees.

In Toronto, Woody Williams allowed no hits over the first 5 1/3 innings and Carlos Delgado drilled a three-run homer as the Blue Jays salvaged the finale of their three-game interleague series, 5-3 over the Atlanta Braves.

Williams (2-4) did not allow a hit until Rafael Belliard singled with one out in the sixth. He gave up three runs and two hits with four walks and four strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings for his first victory since May 11, snapping a personal four-game losing streak.
Alex Gonzalez also homered for the Blue Jays, who snapped a three-game home losing streak. Toronto split six interleague games, winning two of three at Philadelphia before this series.

John Smoltz (6-6), pitching on three days rest for the second time this season, yielded five runs and six hits over seven innings for Atlanta. The Braves dropped four of six interleague games. They were swept at home by the Orioles and lost for the fifth time in their last seven games overall.

In Cleveland, emergency starter Mike Remlinger allowed two hits over six scoreless innings and Willie Greene hit a solo homer to lead the Cincinnati Reds to a 5-2 victory over the Indians to capture the "Battle of Ohio" series.
Making his first start of the season, Remlinger (2-3) walked three and struck out six. He got the call when Pete Schourek was scratched with a sore left tricep.
In Chicago, Wilson Alvarez (5-6) tossed a four-hitter and Lyle Mouton hit a two-run double in the first inning as the White Sox captured the rubber game of their Windy City series with the Cubs, 3-0.
Dave Martinez added his second homer of the series, a solo shot in the seventh, to cap the scoring.
In Kansas City, Jeff King belted his seventh career grand slam in the first inning and the Royals got their fourth win in five games, 6-2 over the Houston Astros.
King's 12th homer of the season extended his hitting streak to 13 games. He is 19-for-44 (.431) with six homers, 12 runs and 15 RBI inn that span.
Jim Pittsley (2-4) allowed two runs and eight hits with four strikeouts in a career-high eight innings. Jeff Montgomery worked a scoreless ninth.

In Milwaukee, Jeromy Burnitz's bases-loaded triple keyed a four-run second inning and Jeff Cirillo had three hits and two RBI as the Brewers rallied past the St Louis Cardinals 8-4 to sweep their interleague series.
Jeff D'Amico (4-3) got the win and Andy Benes (5-3) the loss. The Cardinals have dropped four straight and five of their last six, all in interleague play.
At Florida, Omar Olivares (5-5) pitched a four-hitter for his third complete game of the season and Joe Hall drove in three runs to lead the Detroit Tigers past the Marlins 6-2.

Hall, an outfielder making his first start since July 6, 1995 and second appearance of the season, went 2-for-3, including a two-run single to cap a three-run first inning. The Tigers snapped a five-game losing streak, becoming the last team in the majors to record an interleague win.

In Minnesota, Brad Radke (7-5) allowed two runs and seven hits over 6 2/3 innings and Ron Coomer delivered a bases-clearing double to cap a five-run third inning and lead the Twins to an 8-2 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates.

In Baltimore, Carlos Perez (8-4) pitched his third shutout in his last four starts, all wins after three straight losses, and Sherman Obando homered in the sixth for the game's only run as the Montreal Expos edged the Orioles, 1-0.

In Boston, Shane Mack capped a three-run seventh inning with a two-run single and Jeff Suppan went seven strong innings to win his second straight start as the Red Sox defeated the Philadelphia Phillies, 4-2.
Boston swept the interleague series.
